name: 86 Chaos 17.1.7
label: 86 Chaos 17.1.7
notes: Turns the first mobile toolbar slot into the actual 86Voice button instead of reserving an empty slot beneath a floating overlay.
Wires the toolbar button synchronously to 86Voice through an imperative ref so the tap reaches the voice controller directly.
Requests microphone access with getUserMedia before speech recognition starts and shows a visible permission/error path when access is blocked.
Keeps the old floating trigger on desktop only and removes it from the mobile tap path.
title: 86 Chaos 17.1.7
summary: Rebuilds the mobile microphone as a real first toolbar button with direct 86Voice wiring and explicit microphone-permission handling.
description: Replaces the fragile floating-overlay microphone path with a true bottom-navigation control wired directly to 86Voice, adds explicit microphone access handling, and preserves all 17.1.6 release-gate repairs.
highlights: Voice is now a real first-class mobile navigation button.
The legacy floating mobile microphone can no longer steal or swallow taps.
Microphone permission is explicitly requested and released before recognition begins.
New browser coverage verifies one tap opens 86Voice, requests microphone access, and starts recognition.
